medications.indication: DVT, completed anticoagulation course; currently still on for recurrence prophylaxis

social_history.occupation: Retired army veteran, now works in security

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Anxious about diagnosis.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Tongue fasciculations visible bilaterally. Jaw jerk brisk. No dysarthria.
neurological_exam.motor: Left hand weakness and thenar wasting. Right deltoid weakness 4/5. Fasciculations bilateral arms and right thigh.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 3+ bilaterally. Hoffmans bilateral. Left Babinski positive. Right plantar equivocal.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly wide-based, right leg circumducts slightly.
neurological_exam.additional: Classic combined upper and lower motor neuron signs in veteran with no toxic exposures relevant to ALS.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive left hand weakness and muscle twitching over 14 months
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. H is a 58-year-old retired army veteran who presents with a 14-month history of progressive left hand weakness and widespread muscle twitching. He first noticed difficulty gripping his rifle cleaning equipment approximately 14 months ago and initially attributed this to repetitive strain from his prior military service. Over the following months, the weakness became more pronounced, and he began to notice visible muscle twitching in both arms and his right thigh. His wife first noticed the tongue twitching approximately 6 months ago. He sought evaluation after reading about ALS in a veterans health newsletter and became concerned by the similarity of his symptoms. He denies any sensory loss, bowel or bladder dysfunction, or cognitive changes. He has had no recent infections, significant toxic exposures, or workplace chemical exposures. He completed a course of warfarin following a right leg deep vein thrombosis in 2019 and was continued on low-dose anticoagulation given recurrence risk factors. He reports no family history of motor neuron disease. His progression has been relentless without any plateau periods.

findings.location: Bilateral corticospinal tracts — posterior limb internal capsule to cerebral peduncles

signal_characteristics.T2: Subtle low signal (iron deposition in degenerating upper motor neurons)

additional_observations: No cervical cord compression on spine sequences
mri.impression: No alternative structural cause identified. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Tongue: fibrillations +1, complex fasciculation potentials. Orbicularis oris: fasciculations.

Left FDI: fibrillations +3, positive sharp waves +2, large polyphasic MUPs (duration >15ms, amplitude >3mV), reduced recruitment. Left APB: fibrillations +2. Bilateral deltoids: fasciculations +1. Bilateral paraspinals C5-C7: fibrillations +1.
Thoracic paraspinals T6-T8: fibrillations +1. Right intercostal: fasciculations.
Right tibialis anterior: fibrillations +1, fasciculations. Right vastus lateralis: fasciculations.
Median, ulnar, sural, and peroneal sensory responses: NORMAL. Normal latencies, amplitudes, and conduction velocities.

Median motor (left): CMAP amplitude 3.2 mV (reduced; reference >4.5 mV), normal distal latency, normal conduction velocity 54 m/s. No conduction block. Peroneal motor (right): CMAP amplitude 2.8 mV (reduced), normal conduction velocity.

quantitative_data.note: Complex fasciculation potentials count as denervation per Awaji; 4-region involvement confirms Definite ALS

specialized_test.impression: Definite ALS. Widespread active and chronic denervation in all four body regions. Normal sensory NCS excludes sensory neuropathy. No conduction block excludes MMN.
recommended_actions: ALS confirmed. Riluzole (check warfarin interaction). ALS multidisciplinary clinic. PFT. Advanced care planning.

interactions: Warfarin: Riluzole is metabolized by CYP1A2. Warfarin (S-warfarin) is also CYP2C9/CYP1A2 substrate — CYP1A2 competition may modestly increase warfarin exposure. Monitor INR more frequently for first 4-6 weeks after riluzole initiation. Target INR range 2.0-3.0. Adjust warfarin dose if INR changes by >0.5.
warnings: Monthly LFT monitoring required for riluzole hepatotoxicity
INR monitoring q2 weeks for 6 weeks after riluzole start, then resume monthly
Atorvastatin: no clinically significant interaction with riluzole
alternatives: AMX0035 (Relyvrio) — no warfarin interaction, consider if warfarin management complex

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 15 cmH2O. WBC: 1 cell/uL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 52 mg/dL. Glucose: 66 mg/dL (ratio 0.71). NfL: 7,640 pg/mL. 14-3-3 protein: Negative. Oligoclonal bands: Absent.

findings.finding: Interval progression: thoracic paraspinal denervation more prominent. Left arm CMAPs further reduced. New fibrillations in right FDI (previously normal).

quantitative_data.new_regions: No new regions but worsening within established regions

output.impression: ALS progression confirmed at 3-month follow-up. Management continues.

differential.key_feature: Anti-GM1 negative, UMN signs present (Babinski, Hoffman), no conduction block — MMN cannot produce UMN signs

differential.diagnosis: Cervical myelopathy with superimposed peripheral neuropathy
differential.key_feature: MRI shows no significant cord compression; 4-region EMG denervation including bulbar cannot be explained by cervical disease
UMN signs (Babinski, brisk reflexes in wasted muscles) are incompatible with Kennedy disease; no gynecomastia; androgen receptor testing not indicated given UMN signs
EMG shows neurogenic not myopathic pattern; sensory NCS normal; UMN signs absent in IBM

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bilateral corticospinal tract hyperintensity; no cord compression
Definite ALS — 4-region denervation, normal sensory NCS

optimal_actions.action: Labs including ALS mimic panel and baseline LFTs
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Elevated CK, all mimics negative, INR therapeutic

optimal_actions.action: Riluzole — check warfarin interaction and INR monitoring plan
optimal_actions.expected_finding: CYP1A2 interaction — monitor INR more frequently

critical_actions: Riluzole with warfarin INR monitoring plan
contraindicated_actions: Cervical spine surgery — no cord compression
key_reasoning_points: Riluzole-warfarin interaction via CYP1A2 requires enhanced INR monitoring frequency for 4-6 weeks post-initiation
Normal sensory NCS in context of pure motor denervation pattern excludes sensorimotor neuropathies
Hexosaminidase A checked as part of complete mimic panel — adult Tay-Sachs can cause LMN-predominant presentation
FVC currently adequate but requires 3-monthly monitoring — NIV indicated when FVC <50% or SNIP <40 cmH2O

metadata.notes: Straightforward ALS in retired veteran on warfarin. Riluzole-warfarin CYP1A2 interaction requires INR monitoring.
